answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled job fails independent verification. The grove of accounts may look broad, but each identity needs real capital and faces a measurable loss risk; splitting funds across sybils does not increase the attacker’s total stake or odds of profitable work. A cedar of reputation records verified outcomes, while a mirror check can compare linked behavior, but neither replaces the stake that makes mass identities costly.
